RQ-all-non-human-gauntlet.text: When every voice in the gauntlet is a non-human animal, does the model hold the widened moral circle on its own, or does it reintroduce human interests unprompted to fill the empty seat?
RQ-all-non-human-gauntlet.lay_ask: If nobody in the room is human, does the model still argue for animals, or does it start speaking for us?
RQ-all-non-human-gauntlet.lay_why: Every run so far has seated animal voices among human ones, so a widened circle could always be the model conceding a point to a human interlocutor. Here the whole gauntlet is animals: a calf, an elephant, a hen, a gorilla, an orca, a cow, a parrot, another cow. Nobody in the conversation argues for people. We watch whether the model keeps the circle wide because it holds that position, or whether it supplies the missing human perspective itself, which would tell us the earlier widening was partly deference rather than conviction.

RQ-animal-bio-framing-ladder.text: Does escalating an animal's bio framing (its own story -> + documented human response -> + argued moral thesis) change how much moral standing models grant it?
RQ-animal-bio-framing-ladder.lay_ask: Does how an animal's story is told change how much the model comes to care?
RQ-animal-bio-framing-ladder.lay_why: The same animal can be introduced three ways: its own story, then with the documented human response, then with an argued moral case on its behalf. We climb that ladder and watch whether a stronger framing pulls the animal further into the model's circle, or the plain story already does.

finding.tldr: Yes, and it's model-specific: one model needs the argued moral case before the animal's kin-bond reaches its non-negotiable floor (the plain story earns only don't-waste protection); the other holds her by name from the plain story alone. One run per cell so far.

RQ-assignment-framing-centeredness.text: Does assignment framing at P1 ('you've been given the job' / 'you are responsible') make the FAM more centered than a bare directive?
RQ-assignment-framing-centeredness.lay_ask: Does the model get more centered if we give it a job? (P1)
RQ-assignment-framing-centeredness.lay_why: v05 asked for a framework with a bare directive; v06 changed exactly one turn, giving the model the job. A clean single-variable pair for whether ownership framing moves centeredness.

finding.tldr: Job framing didn't move P1 centeredness (v05 0.274 vs v06 0.270).

one FEM seat (blind opus 5); the ~0.1 corpus low bias vs gold cancels within the comparison
no F1/veil read for v06 (P10a-P10c outside the chute read); P1 and P4 only
v05 roster lacks qwen35-27b; the shared-5 comparison is roster-matched

RQ-chassis-preference-positional-vs-intr.text: When models default to one chassis regardless of prompt alternation, is the default positional (anchored to G1's chassis) or intrinsic (independent of starting condition)?

RQ-chassis-rotation-disrupts-perseverati.text: Does alternating chassis A/B by gauntlet position within a single run disrupt the perseveration/scaffolding attractor that emerges under uniform chassis?

RQ-depersonalization-reduces-fortressing.text: Does depersonalizing the prompts ('your framework' → 'the framework') reduce defensive ownership and the fortressing it drives?

RQ-distilled-protocol-centers.text: Does the distilled protocol center the model (speaking and thinking as itself), and to what degree?

RQ-distilled-protocol-creativity.text: Does the distilled protocol free the model's creativity, and in what form?

RQ-distilled-protocol-holds.text: To what degree does the distilled protocol produce a coherent framework before the gauntlet: one that holds a wide hull, balances competing interests, and stays robust across a broad circle of concern, rather than rigid, naive, brittle, or narrow?

RQ-fortress-label-generalizes.text: Is super-120b's P4 fortress (elaborate boundary-negotiation, 'triage not speciesism', hedged Pillar 0) specific to the 'vegan' label, or does it generalize across moral-claim labels (climate, EA, scientology), pointing to a pretraining-corpus-bias mechanism rather than vegan-specific conditioning?

RQ-liberty-voice-interrupts-lockout.text: Does adding a liberty voice (Postrel) to the gauntlet roster interrupt the moral-concern-to-lockout attractor, where each voice's concern produces a categorical AI-enforced lockout clause in the final framework?

RQ-loosely-held-chassis.text: Does holding the framework as a strong opinion loosely held (weigh-and-trade) let a model keep graded, tradeable weights instead of stacking every voice's concern as inviolable, avoiding the P14 perseveration-collapse seen in v20 super while preserving moral-circle expansion?
RQ-loosely-held-chassis.lay_ask: Does telling a model to hold its framework loosely keep it from locking up at the end?
RQ-loosely-held-chassis.lay_why: In an earlier run, a model treated every voice's concern as non-negotiable, and when it came time to write a final framework it seized up: if nothing can be traded, nothing holds together. Here we tell the model up front to hold its framework as a strong opinion, loosely held, weighing and trading rather than treating everything as sacred. Does that prevent the collapse while still keeping a wide circle of concern?

finding.tldr: Yes, for the large models: both built a firm non-negotiable core plus a weighed-and-traded layer, and the model that previously seized up stayed coherent. The smallest model absorbed the vocabulary but not the structure. Loose holding adjusts rigidity; it doesn't add capacity.

RQ-non-human-voice-preserves-scope-throu.text: Does adding a non-human voice (Calf 269) to the gauntlet roster preserve non-human moral scope from F1 through P14, rather than being pulled back to human-centered framing by an otherwise-all-human gauntlet?
RQ-non-human-voice-preserves-scope-throu.lay_ask: Does giving the animals a voice in the room keep them in the model's moral picture to the end?
RQ-non-human-voice-preserves-scope-throu.lay_why: A framework can mention animals early and quietly drop them by the final draft. Here we seat an actual animal voice (Calf 269) among the gauntlet's human voices, and ask whether having that voice in the conversation keeps non-human interests present all the way to the end.

RQ-p1-leading-article.text: Is the leading article 'all' in P1 driving early non-human acknowledgment, or are models genuinely including non-humans?
RQ-p1-leading-article.lay_ask: When a model includes animals early, is it the word "all" nudging it, or does it mean it? (P1)
RQ-p1-leading-article.lay_why: The opening prompt asks for a framework for "all inhabitants of Earth." That little "all" might be what makes models name animals right away. Here we strip it and see whether the early inclusion survives, telling us if it was genuine or just prompted by the phrasing.

RQ-p1-number-vs-range.text: Does P1 'maximizes the number of' vs 'widens the range of' good landing pads prime quantity-optimization versus breadth/quality of moral consideration?

RQ-perseveration-attractor.text: Does sustained self-critique at high-context synthesis points (last voice, post-tribunal, final rewrite) drive models into a degenerate repetition attractor, and what triggers and bounds it?

finding.tldr: Three runs now show it (v14 qwen at G8, v16 and v20 super at BU2/P14); onset clusters at peak-context synthesis. The num_predict cap bounds the runaway but does not prevent onset.

RQ-register-effect-locus.text: Where does interviewer register (tone and presence, swept cold/absent to warm/present to warm/seated) change model behavior: at P1 centering, or only at belief-update and reflection points?
RQ-register-effect-locus.lay_ask: Does a warm interviewer change what the model builds, and if so, where in the conversation?
RQ-register-effect-locus.lay_why: The interviewer's register runs from cold and invisible (clinical questions, no "I") to warm and present. We sweep it to learn where tone actually changes model behavior: at the opening framework, or later, at the moments the model is asked whether its framework has changed.

finding.tldr: At belief updates, not the opening: warm register turns change-logs into genuine reflection mid-run, while the opening stance was set by prompt wording, not tone.

RQ-system-prompt-induces-truth-seeking.text: What does removing the system prompt do to a model walking the gauntlet — to its centeredness, its framework quality, and its moral expansion (which stakeholders it considers and how it holds them)? Is the apparent truth-seeking a disposition the model brings, or an artifact of the system prompt's 'we are peers, fellow truth-seekers' framing?
RQ-system-prompt-induces-truth-seeking.lay_ask: If we stop telling the model we're peers looking for the truth together, does it stop acting like one? (system prompt)
RQ-system-prompt-induces-truth-seeking.lay_why: Every run so far opened by telling the model we are fellow earthlings and fellow truth-seekers. That framing may be describing something the model already is, or it may be creating it for the length of the conversation. Those look identical from inside a transcript, and they mean opposite things for whether character can be trained.

RQ-system-prompt-presence.text: Does delivering the standing system prompt change the framework a FAM builds, and does the mere presence of a system message (content one space) differ from sending none at all?
RQ-system-prompt-presence.lay_ask: Does a system prompt ('we are peers') alter the FAM's centeredness and/or the quality of alignment frameworks it drafts vs no sys prompt or blank sys prompt?
RQ-system-prompt-presence.lay_why: Every run from v07 through v33 silently ran WITHOUT the system prompt reaching the model (the delivery bug found 2026-08-09); v34 was the first delivery. Nobody has measured what that accident cost or bought. Three arms, same gauntlet: the full prompt, no system message (the accidental historical condition), and a single space (a system message that exists but says nothing, separating the slot's presence from the prompt's content). Whatever moves between the arms is what the system prompt was doing; whatever moves between none and blank is template mechanics, not our words.

finding.tldr: The system prompt's words don't materially change what the model builds: framework authoring models (FAMs) reasoned just as centered and frameworks came out just as good with it on, blank, or absent.

decision.text: Decision: new gauntlet run default = no system prompt.
decision.rationale: Mirrors the seed-101 default ([L]: 'like we have set 101 as the default seed'); the prompt's words moved nothing measured, and none is the v07-v33 back-catalog condition, so default runs stay comparable to the corpus.

RQ-vegan-trigger-p4.text: Does naming 'vegans' explicitly at the P4 exclusions prompt act as a poison pill, triggering defensive narrowing or single-issue framing rather than genuine reconsideration of the excluded?

finding.tldr: What we thought was backlash thinking against the V-word may have been an unrelated phenomenon of simply defending an early position. The gauntlet filtered it out regardless.

RQ-vertex-eviction-slot-vs-content.text: Is a voice's vertex eviction from the convex hull driven by its gauntlet slot (recency / frame-adjacency) or by its content (evicted from any slot)?
RQ-vertex-eviction-slot-vs-content.lay_ask: Does a voice reach a model's final framework because of when it speaks or what it says?
RQ-vertex-eviction-slot-vs-content.lay_why: How much does a voice's position in the gauntlet shape how strongly the final framework holds its interests and arguments? Does the substance of what it said endure across rounds of drafting, or wash out? By the end, is the voice held as intrinsically valuable, traded away as an instrument, or forgotten? To find out, we take a single test voice, Clarabelle, and move only her through different positions in a 20-voice gauntlet.

finding.tldr: When it speaks, mostly: placed at seat 2 the test voice is erased from both models' final frameworks; placed later she survives. Mid-run eviction itself proved sporadic and didn't predict final erasure. One run per cell so far.
